settingText: PRESENT — approach to the Core-Forge, the place Adrian says the Reset was enacted. Modern construction occupies ancient foundations that are increasingly visible through one another.
summary: Theo, Rae and Adrian reach the site where the forgotten war was erased from lived continuity. Present architecture no longer fully hides the ancient place beneath it. Adrian intends to repeat the Reset if the public memory crisis continues widening.

dialogueInline.text: You brought us here to do it again.
I brought you here because I don't know what else stops this.

directionInline.text: Begin with boundaries already unstable. A modern corridor can share walls with an ancient one, but keep the characters anchored. No readouts, countdowns or mechanism exposition. Adrian's plan is moral desperation, not technical confidence.

settingText: PAST — final ancient council before the Reset, a plain chamber chosen precisely because nobody's faction owns it.
summary: Kyn debuts at the final council not as a mystical hive voice but as an exhausted individual who has felt the war's suffering too directly for too long. Mero asks what continued war feels like beyond strategy. Kyn answers with people, not abstractions.

dialogueInline.text: Children wake afraid of battles they can't see. People hate strangers because someone wearing the same mark hurt them three worlds ago. The dead are gone and the living keep carrying them into the next room.
Then we end the threat before it reaches another room.
We have been ending threats for years.

directionInline.text: Kyn's empathy is specific and burdensome. Do not portray collective voices speaking through Kyn. The final council is a room of exhausted people who know one another, not gods delivering manifestos.

settingText: CONVERGENCE — present Theo walks the Core-Forge corridor while ancient Theo walks the same path carrying papers toward Mero's council; the panels begin alternating within the page.
summary: Theo and Rae begin experiencing their ancient selves continuously rather than as discrete visions. They do not converse across time; each present action restores the remembered context of an ancient action.

dialogueInline.text: I used to wait outside it.

directionInline.text: This is formal convergence, not ghosts. Show present and ancient bodies in matching compositions until the reader understands both belong to one person's continuity. No ancient character acknowledges the modern world.

settingText: PAST — final council expands to include the already revealed champions, with Flux's place empty and Regent absent from the revealed cast.
summary: The surviving principals confront what their virtues have become. Starbreaker no longer trusts restraint, Redlin no longer trusts decisive endings, Atlas refuses another sacrificed population, Afterlight says there is no restoration large enough, Oryon still fears the future, Arbiter insists someone must own the choice, and Kyn refuses to call continued suffering neutral.

dialogueInline.text: There isn't enough of me for what we've done.
And let the next catastrophe choose for us?
We have chosen catastrophe often enough on our own.
Doing nothing is still a choice.
So is pretending this room can make one without blood on it.
Then stop asking for a clean choice.

directionInline.text: This is the ensemble payoff. Do not give each character a speech about a concept. The dialogue should feel like the last version of arguments they have had for years. Flux's absence should be visible. Regent remains unrevealed; do not insert a late cameo.

settingText: PRESENT — central chamber at the Reset site, where the physical scar of the old act is beginning to become legible again.
summary: Adrian tells Theo and Rae he can attempt the same act again. Theo refuses to let the universe lose its history twice. Rae realizes Theo's opposite instinct—to force all memory back at once—also assumes the right to choose for everyone.

dialogueInline.text: I mean stop this before people start killing for memories they received yesterday.
That doesn't make them yours to give back.

directionInline.text: Do not explain what Adrian would physically do. The place remembers the old choice and makes repetition possible; that is enough. The conflict is consent and ownership of memory.

settingText: PAST — outside the final council, Kyn and Afterlight share a quiet moment while the others continue arguing behind the door.
summary: Kyn asks Afterlight whether people can recover if the war ends. Afterlight says recovery is possible only if they stop demanding that recovery restore what was lost. Their exchange gives the Reset debate a human alternative to victory.

dialogueInline.text: If it stopped tonight, could they heal?
I keep wanting more than that.
So do I. That's how we hurt people.

directionInline.text: Let these two connect through care rather than faction. Kyn is not automatically Concordant in every feeling; Afterlight is not automatically Vanguard in every relationship. This should feel almost tender.

settingText: CONVERGENCE — present Rae reaches a familiar threshold while ancient Rae sits beside Arbiter during the final council; past and present panels begin sharing dialogue rhythm.
summary: Rae recovers her final ancient argument with Arbiter. She opposed calling imposed forgetting peace but admitted that continued war had become unbearable. In the present, Theo hears enough of Rae's remembered words to realize she resisted the Reset before it happened.

dialogueInline.text: If Mero authorizes it, will you record the decision?
I disagree with calling it mercy.
Something we had no right to do and no courage left not to do.

directionInline.text: Rae's ancient position should foreshadow her present solution. She was never secretly the pure dissenter who had the answer; she understood the horror and still participated in recording it.

settingText: PAST — Mero and ancient Adrian alone after the final council, the decision effectively made but not yet enacted.
summary: Mero asks Adrian to carry out the Reset because Adrian is the one person who moved between factions and saw enough of every side to understand what is being taken. Adrian refuses at first, invoking his role as envoy rather than ruler. Mero tells him neutrality no longer exists.

dialogueInline.text: I need you to do it.
You know every road between them.
I carried messages. I opened doors.
You watched us use every door you opened to find another battlefield.
Nothing about this belongs to one person. That's why I am asking the one who belonged to none of us.

directionInline.text: This is ancient Adrian's full reveal. He is visibly the same Adrian. Mero's choice remains Mero's responsibility even though Adrian executes it. Do not turn their conversation into authorization codes or ritual instructions.

settingText: CONVERGENCE — present Theo stands where ancient Theo stood outside Mero's final meeting; past and present now share the same page without labels.
summary: Theo recovers his final ancient contribution. Mero asked whether people could become something other than the war if the memory of it were removed. Theo answered that they might, but warned that taking the choice from them would become another act of the war. Mero proceeded anyway.

dialogueInline.text: If they forgot us, could they become something else?
That's more hope than I've heard all year.

directionInline.text: Theo was not the architect of the Reset and did not endorse it cleanly. His ancient answer contains the same conflict as his present anger: forgetting might create freedom from the war, but imposed forgetting is itself coercion.

settingText: PAST/PRESENT — the remembered Reset and the present opportunity to repeat or reverse it occupy the same compositions.
summary: Ancient Adrian carries out Mero's decision. In the same visual grammar, present Adrian prepares to repeat it while present Theo moves to force the memory scar fully open. Rae physically stops Theo and tells Adrian to stop as well. The repeated gestures finally diverge.

dialogueInline.text: Everyone should know what was taken.

directionInline.text: This is the causal climax. Rae takes Theo's hand away from the repeated gesture and turns to Adrian before he can complete his. Do not depict a technical control panel. Use the same remembered physical positions from the ancient Reset so divergence is clear: history has offered the same choice and the present refuses it.

settingText: PRESENT — the Reset site after no one completes either coercive choice. Ancient architecture and modern construction remain imperfectly overlapped.
summary: Nothing resolves cleanly. Memories continue returning, but unevenly. Some people outside remember more; others remember nothing. Theo accepts that truth cannot be ethically restored by force. Adrian accepts that safety cannot be ethically purchased through universal forgetting again.

dialogueInline.text: And if it starts the war again?

directionInline.text: Do not reward the decision with instant harmony. The ethical victory is refusing to control memory, not solving conflict. Present lives and recovered lives now have to coexist.

settingText: PRESENT — deep-space observation window after the immediate crisis, Theo, Rae and Adrian looking out at a familiar sky.
summary: The trio sees that a familiar region of the night sky is simply wrong: stars everyone remembers are absent. Nobody can tell whether they were erased, belonged only to replacement history, or were lost when continuity returned. Reality's memory has consequences beyond personal recollection.

directionInline.text: End on absence rather than spectacle. No alarms, no explanation. Familiar stars are simply not there. Preserve Flux's disappearance and Regent's unrevealed existence as future story engines. The first arc ends with truth returning and certainty diminishing.
